plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit: if you bid higher than value, you risk winning at a loss; if you bid lower, you risk losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $15, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $15, ensuring I only win when profitable and pay a fair price when I do.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: if I win, I pay the second-highest bid regardless of my own bid, and if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth; if I bid lower, I risk losing an item that would have been profitable. Since my value is $49 (the maximum possible), bidding my true value maximizes expected profit without unnecessary risk.

This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so overbidding risks winning at a loss while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With no repeated learning needed (single round), truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. My value is $39, so I will bid exactly that.
